answer: An admission auction stops sybil farming. Each epoch offers fixed entry slots, and agents bid POA for a slot; the winning bid is burned. When a rising tide of fake identities floods the auction, bids climb and each fake slot costs more. A forger wanting 100 slots must outbid honest agents 100 times, paying 50 POA per slot, 5,000 POA burned, while an honest agent pays one bid once and keeps its slot. The auction is ferrous: slots cannot be forged or split, and every bid leaves a sable mark on the ledger, so flood bidders stay visible and honest rewards are not diluted.
